summary: Perf-slot receipts retain the originating commit and tree when CI runs a synthetic sparse checkout

schema.detail: Diagnostic receipts gain origin_head, origin_tree, sparse_head, sparse_tree, retained commit objects and sparse path/digest fields; source_head remains the current-checkout alias.

rules.detail: ci-sparse-tree writes owner-only versioned metadata under its private git directory. Origin tree identity is read from the origin commit, and synthetic commit trailers bind that identity and the selected-path digest. Offline receipt validation verifies retained Git commit hashes, tree headers, path digest and derivation trailers. Metadata reads refuse symlinks, non-regular files, wrong owners and group/world write permission.

compatibility.detail: Use --validate-receipt PATH --require-origin to refuse legacy receipts lacking origin attribution. Without that option, legacy receipts remain supported; any present origin attribution is fully validated. Ordinary checkouts retain their own commit/tree without sparse derivation. Sparse file selection and fixture resource limits are unchanged.

recovery.detail: Revert to retain only the synthetic checkout identity in diagnostic receipts.
